name: Microsoft Office apps
summary: Word, Excel and PowerPoint, on the desktop and in the browser, sold by subscription as part of Microsoft 365.

factors: Everyone you work with sends, and expects, .docx, .xlsx and .pptx
Macros, Power Query, data models and add-ins exist only in Excel
Templates, styles and fonts that render differently elsewhere
Real-time co-authoring only works on files stored in OneDrive or SharePoint

export.summary: Your documents are already files in a documented format. There is nothing to export, only compatibility to check.

methods.name: Keep the files
methods.detail: Office files open directly in every alternative listed here. Download anything that lives only in OneDrive or SharePoint so that you hold local copies.

methods.name: Batch-convert to OpenDocument (optional)
methods.detail: LibreOffice can convert whole folders from the command line (soffice --headless --convert-to odt *.docx). Only worth doing for documents you will keep editing; archives can stay as they are.

caveats: Files protected with sensitivity labels or rights management must be unprotected while you still have a licence
Install metric-compatible fonts such as Carlito and Caladea so that layouts do not reflow
Desktop Office keeps working in read-only mode after a subscription ends, but do not rely on it for the migration

paths.verdict: The default choice for individuals and for anyone who mostly works alone on documents.

import.summary: Opens Office files directly. Test your ten most complex documents first: long Word files with tracked changes, spreadsheets with pivot tables or macros, and animated slide decks are where differences show.

links.label: Feature comparison with Microsoft Office (Document Foundation wiki)

transfers: Styles, charts and the great majority of formulas
lost: Power Query, Power Pivot and data-model features

paths.verdict: Best when you exchange Office files with outsiders all day and need them to come back intact.

import.summary: It works on .docx, .xlsx and .pptx natively, so there is no conversion step. Put the files on your file platform and edit them.

transfers: Documents, spreadsheets and presentations, in their original formats
Co-editing in the browser, once connected to a file platform
lost: All VBA macros (it has a separate JavaScript macro system)
Power Query, Power Pivot and data-model features
Some advanced Word features, such as complex mail merges and fields

paths.verdict: The natural pick if you are moving to Nextcloud and want a fully open stack.

import.summary: Same engine as LibreOffice, so the same compatibility testing applies. Files stay in their original format unless you choose to convert them.

transfers: Co-editing in the browser, once connected to a file platform
lost: Power Query, Power Pivot and data-model features

paths.verdict: For people who work alone on Office files and want a desktop app that keeps them in Office formats.

import.summary: It edits .docx, .xlsx and .pptx natively, so there is nothing to convert: install it and open your files. Test your most complex documents first, and keep LibreOffice to hand for legacy .doc files, which it opens but cannot save.

transfers: Documents, spreadsheets and presentations, in their original formats
Fonts, images and tables, with Office-style layout
lost: Power Query, Power Pivot and data-model features
